:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 14.11.2021 at about 2.30 p.m. petitioner was proceeding as pedestrian on extreme left side of the road near 9th Main, 11th Cross, near Shanimahathma SCCH-5 Temple Road, Nagapura, Bengaluru, at that time, all of a sudden a car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-P-8138 ridden by respondent No.1 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Pristine Hospital, Bengaluru and spent a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment charges.

3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 60 years, hale and healthy, working as Agriculturist and Cooli, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is not in a position to do his normal work, suffered a lot mentally, financially and physically.

Out of this accident crime No.108/2021 is registered against the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-P-8138 before the SCCH-5 Rajajinagar Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.12,55,000/- with interest.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared through counsel, but not filed written statement.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to take all the defences under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, it is not a proper and necessary party to the said case, as the car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-P-8138 has not at all involved in the alleged accident.

Further submitted that, claim made by the petitioner is exorbitant,
excessive, imaginary and without any basis.
SCCH-5 Further submitted that, liability of this this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further driver of the car did not possess valid and effective driving licence.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

sentences.text:
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 14.11.2021 at abut 2.30 p.m. when petitioner was a pedestrian near 9th Main, 11th Cross, Shanimahathma Temple Road, Nagapura,
Bengaluru, at that time, Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 02-P-8138 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
SCCH-5 3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Balachandra V. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Pristine Hospital as PW-2 and marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- SCCH-5 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of statement of petitioner is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
9 . Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined Dr.Balachandra V. Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Pristine Hospital is examined as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, statement of petitioner, sketch, spot mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of SCCH-5 the accident dated 14.11.2021 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.
Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not not taken any Huchhegowda vs Lalitha B.S on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46804938/
3 endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 14.11.2021 at about 2.30 p.m. when he was walking on left side of the road near 9th Main,
11th Cross, near Shanimahathma Temple Road, Nagapura, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
SCCH-5 11
. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-P-8138.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right leg communited fracture distal third tibia extra articular, right leg fracture lateral malleolus, for which, he underwent surgeries in the form of ORIF right distal third tibia with 10 holed LCP and screws and ORIF lateral malleolus with rush nail.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound SCCH-5 certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11 issued by Pristine Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 14.11.2021 to 19.11.2021.

Further he has furnished medical bills amounting to Rs.1,31,736/- marked as Ex.P.9, advance receipts marked as Ex.P.10.
13.

Further Dr.Balachandra V. Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Pristine Hospital is examined as PW-2 and exhibited disability certificate marked as Ex.P.13, copy of MLC Extract is marked as Ex.P.14, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.15 and inpatient and outpatient files are marked as Ex.P.16.
Further he has assessed total disability of right lower limb is 30.39%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, fractures are united and he has assessed only the physial disability.

Under such circumstances, considering the SCCH-5 nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 10% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 30.39% of right lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 60 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1959 and the alleged accident is occurred on 14.11.2021, accordingly relying on Ex.P.12 his age is considered about 63 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 7 is applicable as per decision reported SCCH-5 in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 15. As per his case, he was working as agriculturist and coolie, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to Huchhegowda vs Lalitha B.S on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46804938/
4 the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.11, petitioner was admitted in Pristine Hospital as inpatient from 14.11.2021 to 19.11.2021 i.e., for 5 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,250/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,375/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
17. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.9 medical bills for Rs.1,31,736/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for SCCH-5 this treatment is considered.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated i.e., Dr.S.K.Karthik has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 14.11.2021.

So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained swelling, tenderness and crepitus present over distal third of right leg and right ankle joint, abrasion present over dorsum of 4 th and 5th toes of right foot.

Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Balachandra Rao H.G.
for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 18.
Per contra except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
19. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of Future Income 1,19,700-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 Huchhegowda vs Lalitha B.S on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46804938/
5 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges SCCH-5 4.
Medical Expenses 1,31,736-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6.
Loss of income during laid up 2,375-00 period Total 2,98,811-00 20.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,98,811/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. Ofcourse during the course of arguments, respondent No.2 counsel argued that, Rs.60,000/-
was paid by the respondent for causing of the accident and prays to deduct the said amount, but towards payment of the said amount, there is no evidence on respondent side, hence said arguments by the respondent No.2 have not support in any manner.
SCCH-5 22.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2414003121P104172432 which is valid for the period from 19.08.2021 to 18.08.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 14.11.2021 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that,
respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH-5 The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,98,811/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Eight Thousand Eight Hundred Eleven Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
